item: A lesson and a shipped-log entry are each a new file, so parallel PRs stop re-conflicting LESSONS.md and its ceiling
key_paths: scripts/ledger_fold.py; scripts/lessons.py; tests/test_ledger_fragments.py; docs/ledger/lessons.d/; docs/ledger/shipped_log.d/; CLAUDE.md
summary: Every PR that carried a lesson appended it to the tail of LESSONS.md and raised the shared _LESSONS_LINE_CEILING, and appended its entry to SHIPPED_LOG.md, so every landing re-conflicted every other open PR in those places (five PRs, each pair conflicting, on 2026-10-06). The shipped rows had already moved to one file per row; this does the same for the other two archives. A lesson is now docs/ledger/lessons.d/<date>-<slug>.md (python scripts/lessons.py --new SLUG) and a shipped-log entry docs/ledger/shipped_log.d/<date>-<slug>.md (python scripts/ledger_fold.py new-log SLUG); lessons.py searches, indexes and shows the archive and the fragments together (an archive entry by its line, a fragment by its file name, because a line number in a growing set of files is not stable). scripts/ledger_fold.py check validates every fragment and bounds one lesson at LESSON_FRAGMENT_MAX_LINES = 200 (the median lesson is 14 lines and the 95th percentile 51), and fold, a release ritual, appends them in name order in binary and LF, deletes them and sets _LESSONS_LINE_CEILING to the real count, so the ceiling moves only at a fold. Protocol rule (5a)(b) in CLAUDE.md and the LESSONS.md header say so (CLAUDE.md ceiling 792 to 796; LESSONS.md stays at 13,644 because the header edit is line-neutral). Open PRs that already append to LESSONS.md keep working, because the ratchet is unchanged; their next lesson is a file.
